sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident that occurred on 12.9.2023.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 12.9.2023 at about 7.00 to 7.30 a.m. the petitioner was proceeding on the motor cycle bearing No. KA-59-J-3467 and when he reached near Guest line circle, Attibele,
at that time the driver of lorry bearing No. KA-04-D-2823 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle and came to the wrong side and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Oxford Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was admitted as inpatient and he has spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as mechanic and earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondent No.1 owner of the vehicle remained absent hence, placed exparte.

Respondent No.2 - insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the goods carrying comprehensive policy to the vehicle bearing No. KA-04-D-2823 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to proof of the policy.
This respondent has specifically denies the occurrence, mode of the accident and also involvement of lorry bearing No. KA-04-D-2823.
The respondent No.2 contended that the driver of the lorry was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

Further denied the age,
avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:

wound certificate and charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 9.

After the registering of FIR the spot mahazar is conducted by the IO and the accident spot is near to the U turn.

These documents evidentiates the occurrence of the accident and Ex.P8 being the wound certificate establishes the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident.

Ex.P9 is the charge sheet wherein after detailed Muddulapalli Ramanamurthy vs Sukanya N on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196474769/

10.

The contents of Ex.P2 & 1 is in consonance with the contents of petition about the rash and negligence driving by the driver of lorry bearing No. KA- 04-D-2823.
11.

The respondent No.1 owner is exparte and the respondent No.2 -insurance company even after sufficient opportunity has not lead any evidence by leading the rebuttal evidence in support of their defence.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner of the offending vehicle remained exparte and has not denied the alleged negligence.
12. The Ex.P8 is wound certificate and Ex.P11 being the discharge summary wherein supported the case of the petitioner about the alleged injuries and treatment.
The contents of Ex.P5 police intimation, Ex.P9 charge sheet corroborates with the contents of complaint.
Ex.P9 charge sheet is filed against the driver of lorry bearing No. KA-04-D-2823 for the offence punishable under Sec. 279 & 338 of IPC R/w. Sec. 187 of IMV Act.

By producing these documents, the petitioner prima-facie established the occurrence of accident and also the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending lorry bearing No.KA-04-D-2823.
13.

Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-9 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of lorry bearing No. KA-04-D-2823.

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima- facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.

The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. The registration of FIR and filing of the charge- sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of lorry bearing No. KA-04-D-2823 resulting in petitioner sustaining injuries.
During the course of cross examination of petitioner, except a suggestion nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioner.
There are no material evidence to prove that the petitioner's negligence was the reason for the said accident.
15. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 12.9.2023 which is caused by the driver of the lorry bearing No. KA-04-D-2823.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:

Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 37 years.
The Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P10 shows that the petitioner was born on 25.4.1986.
The accident took place in the year 2023.

As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P11 petitioner was admitted to Oxford Medical College Hospital on 12.9.2023 and discharged on 3.10.2023 and it shows that he sustained comminuted fracture base of 1 st metatarsal medial cuneiform fracture + lis francs injury right and he underwent procedure of ORIF with holed mini fragment plate+ K wire + cortical screw under SA.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.50,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P12, amounting to Rs.81,898/-.
These bills are not disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieve these bills.
These bills are supported with Ex.P11 discharge summary.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle by rounding off the same i.e., Rs.82,000/- under this head.
c) Loss of income during laid up period: The petitioner has stated that he was working as mechanic and earning Rs.40,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.
In the absence of any document the notional income of the petitioner is considered in the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P11- the petitioner was admitted to Oxford medical college Hospital totally for 21 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total four months period including 6 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.

So,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 4 months = Rs.64,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr. S.A.
Somashekara, working as Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW.2, through him OPD book and X-ray are marked at Ex.P.16 & 17.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained comminuted fracture base of 1st metatarsal + medial cuneiform fracture + lisfranes injury right.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered total disability of 44% to the right lower limb and 22% to the whole body disability.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
Further PW.2 has also stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants, which may costs Rs.40,000/-.
According to the petitioner he was working as mechanic and suffered with comminuted fracture base of 1st metatarsal + medial cunieform fracture + lisfranes injury right.
The injury is on right lower limb and it effects the walking and daily life style of the petitioner which in turn certainly effects on the work of the petitioner.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 17% to the whole body.
The petitioner has produced his Aadhar card which is marked at Ex.P10, as per this document the petitioner was aged 37 years.

As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '15'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 15 X 17% =Rs.4,89,600/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P11 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 21 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P8 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of injuries and the period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 21 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the injuries as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.21,000/- in total.
g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
suffered with comminuted fracture base of 1st metatarsal + medial cuneiform fracture + lis franes injury right.
The injury is on right lower limb and it effects the walking and daily life style of the petitioner which in turn certainly effects on the work of the petitioner.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.60,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses: PW.3 stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which may cost around Rs.40,000/-.
By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 50,000/-
b. Towards medical expenses Rs. 82,000/- c. Towards loss of income during Rs.

laid up period d.
Towards disability Rs. 4,89,600/-
e. Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 50,000/-

17. Liability:- According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the lorry bearing No. KA-04-D-2823.
No other grounds are made out by the respondent No.2 insurance company to consider the contributory negligence by the petitioner or violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1.

Hence, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. except on the amount awarded under the head of future medical expenses.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
18.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total  compensation amount of Rs.8,46,600/-
(Rupees Eight lakhs forty six thousand six hundred only).
The petitioner is entitled for the interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (excluding on the amount awarded under future medical expenses), from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
Further it is clarified that the amount awarded under the head of future medical expenses shall not carries any interest.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of total compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the same to be released in favour of petitioner through E- payment on his proper identification and remaining 25% to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in his name.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
